summary.intent: Plan, verify, and execute phase 64 of CipherBox (Rotation Soundness — Revocation Guarantees), then ship it. The phase fills four engine.ts seams and fixes three confirmed rotation bugs (D-02 re-seal, D-06 node-identity, D-07 ordering).
summary.outcome: Planning fully completed and verified (8 plans / 6 waves, all 5 requirements + 7 decisions covered, passed plan-checker iteration 2 after fixing 1 blocker and 2 warnings). Wave 1 execution completed (64-01 node-identity, 64-02 mergeChildren, 64-03 mintFileKeyOnRotate), but the transcript ends mid-session during wave 1 post-gate typecheck cleanup after a lint-staged stash-pop conflict; waves 2–6 and /ship-phase were not reached.

repo: engine.ts in packages/sdk-core is a single-file bottleneck — waves 2–5 (64-04 through 64-07) must run sequentially because they all modify it; only wave 1 (disjoint files) can parallelize
tsconfig.build.json excludes src/**/*.test.ts, so test file type errors are completely invisible to CI — only an explicit tsc --noEmit against the full tsconfig catches them
tsup (esbuild) does not typecheck — it bundles only; pnpm build in sdk-core/sdk does not catch type errors
The GSD commit helper returns a false-negative 'commit_failed' JSON even when the commit succeeds; verify with git log --oneline -1 rather than the helper's return value
Worktrees are unusable for GSD execution in this monorepo: fresh worktrees have no node_modules so tests and typecheck fail or require a multi-minute pnpm install, plus api:generate leak risk
plan-phase never auto-commits PATTERNS.md — the orchestrator must commit it alongside VALIDATION.md as a manual step
Concurrent agent spawns (pattern-mapper agent + background commit) cause lint-staged 'could not write index' races — always wait for commits to finish before spawning new agents
The docker stack uses redis on port 6380 (non-standard); API dev server runs on port 3000; Wave 6 sdk-e2e requires both the docker stack and the API dev server live
The RESEARCH.md Open Questions section must be renamed '## Open Questions (RESOLVED)' with inline markers before execution — the plan-checker enforces this as a blocker
VALIDATION.md can be written as a skeleton during plan-phase but must be fully populated with per-task rows and nyquist_compliant: true before the checker passes

code.finding: sealChildReadKey seals under the child's own pre-rotation key due to a legacy 'parentReadKey' misnomer — the D-02 re-seal fix belongs out-of-band in rotateReadFromNode (the BFS caller) under the parent's new readKey', not inside rotateOne
D-01: '?? PLACEHOLDER_WRITE_KEY' fallback must be deleted; nodeIpnsPrivateKey absence should throw (fail-closed publishing)
D-07 ordering bug: completedNodeIds.add fires before reMintGrantsRootedAt at L391 — must be swapped so grant re-mint completes before the node is marked done
D-07 resume guard short-circuits without calling verifySubtreeClean; should be replaced with frontier-rebuilding resume to ensure convergence
Stale doc comment 'mark contentRekeyPending' — cosmetic, the actual marker is deferred to Phase 65 per the schema-freeze constraint

Four named throwing stubs — mintFileKeyOnRotate, reMintGrantsRootedAt, mergeConcurrentChildren, verifySubtreeClean — are Phase 64's primary deliverables; signatures are frozen, only bodies need filling

@ts-expect-error directive was placed above await expect() instead of directly above the updateFolderMetadataAndPublish() call — caused 'unused directive' errors while the real TS2345 fired below; directives must sit on the line immediately before the erroring expression
CryptoError was imported from @cipherbox/core but actually lives in @cipherbox/crypto; the test passed at runtime only because toThrow(undefined) matches any throw, hiding the wrong import

mergeChildren stub (was never/throwing) is a Phase-64 deliverable alongside mergeConcurrentChildren — both fill the CAS-409 three-way merge path; plan 64-02 fills mergeChildren, plan 64-06 fills mergeConcurrentChildren

workflow: Recovery from lint-staged stash-pop conflict: restore the conflicted file from HEAD with git checkout HEAD -- <file>, move stash-garbage untracked dirs aside (do not delete — may be legitimate work), then re-commit on a clean tree to prevent another pop-conflict

Before retrying a failed commit, always inspect git stash list and check for old stashes — lint-staged pops the most recent stash on exit, which can be a completely unrelated stash if any concurrent operation created one
API surface regen can return 0 symbols when the artifact is stale/empty; in that case skip it and rely on RESEARCH.md and PATTERNS.md which carry exact line numbers from live code reads

When running multiple git-writing operations (agent commits + orchestrator commits), serialize them strictly — even background-flagged commits can hold the index long enough to block concurrent lint-staged runs
Plan-checker should be re-spawned (not resumed) for re-verification iterations to get a fresh read of the updated artifacts; the checker is stateless and cheap

friction: lint-staged stash-pop conflict during wave 1 post-gate fixup commit: old stash@{1} (phase 3 planning WIP) was popped, conflicted with STATE.md, and dumped unrelated untracked dirs (tests/e2e/, 06.1-webapp-automation-testing/) into the working tree — required manual conflict resolution
First VALIDATION.md commit failed with 'could not write index' — transient git index race caused by pattern-mapper agent running a concurrent background git operation at the same time

plan-checker returned 1 blocker + 2 warnings requiring a full revision cycle (RESEARCH.md missing RESOLVED markers, VALIDATION.md TBD placeholder, 64-07 missing no-double-bump guard) before verification passed

tsup build does not typecheck — required a separate explicit tsc --noEmit step to surface 2 phase-64 type errors (misplaced @ts-expect-error in registration.test.ts, wrong CryptoError import in move-reseal.test.ts) that were invisible to the normal build

CryptoError imported from wrong package (@cipherbox/core vs @cipherbox/crypto) in the move-reseal test — the test passed at runtime because toThrow(undefined) matches any throw, masking the import bug
API surface regen returned 0 symbols — the artifact was empty/stale and provided no value for the planner
